---
title: "8.5 Performance"
order: 5
---

Every figure on this page names the population it was measured on. Two kinds are measured,
and they are not the same: the **model's ranking**, on the held-out
{{< var li.test_share >}} of the booked book — {{< var li.n_test >}} accounts the model never
saw while it was fitted, {{< var li.n_events_holdout >}} of them positive
([8.2](data.qmd#li-split)) — and the **offered cohort**, which is drawn from the whole book and
is mostly the model's training rows.

## The headline {#li-headline}

{{< include ../../_generated/li-headline.md >}}

`train.py` asserts six gates ([8.9](gate.qmd)). Two measure the model on held-out accounts:

- **AUC** {{< var li.auc >}} against a gate of {{< var li.gate.auc_min >}}, a margin of
  {{< var li.gate.auc_margin >}}.
- **Top-quintile lift** {{< var li.lift >}}× against {{< var li.gate.lift_min >}}×: the
  held-out fifth with the highest probability — {{< var li.top20.n >}} accounts — holds
  {{< var li.top20.events >}} positives, a rate of {{< var li.top20.rate >}} against a base
  rate of {{< var li.base_rate_holdout >}}, and {{< var li.top20.capture >}} of all held-out
  positives.

The other four check the offered cohort against the book, and the last column of the table
says whether each can fail. Only "accounts offered" can. The aggregate ROE gate cannot fail
**by construction**: it is an equity-weighted mean of per-loan ROEs that each clear the same
hurdle. The PD and utilisation gates cannot fail **on this book**: the PD ceiling is the
book's median PD, {{< var li.cohort_gate.pd.book_median >}}, which here lies below the mean,
{{< var li.book_pd >}}, so any cohort under the ceiling has a lower mean than the book; and an
amount needs utilisation above `target_util`, so every account with one is at
{{< var li.cohort_gate.util.min_amount >}} or more (median
{{< var li.cohort_gate.util.median_amount >}}, mean
{{< var li.cohort_gate.util.mean_amount >}}), above the book's mean of
{{< var li.book_util >}}. A book whose PD were skewed the other way, or whose mean utilisation
were above `target_util`, could fail them; this one cannot. That is finding 1
([8.7](limitations.qmd)).

### How firm each result is

From {{< var li.boot.n >}} bootstrap resamples of the held-out accounts, with the platform
seed, as for D4, D5 and D7:

- **AUC: met.** The interval, {{< var li.boot.auc.lo >}} to {{< var li.boot.auc.hi >}},
  has its low end just above the {{< var li.gate.auc_min >}} gate;
  {{< var li.boot.auc_below_gate >}} of resamples fall below it.
- **Lift: met, firmly.** The interval, {{< var li.boot.lift.lo >}}× to
  {{< var li.boot.lift.hi >}}×, lies wholly above the gate; {{< var li.boot.lift_below_gate >}}
  of resamples fall below it. But single inputs pass this gate too (below).

## The ceiling {#li-ceiling}

Because the data are generated, the best possible ranking is known: rank the accounts by the
generator's own line-increase logit without its noise term (`wiki/facts/ceiling.py`, the only
code in this documentation that reads the generator's truth; it uses the stored, rounded
on-book utilisation where the generator used the unrounded value, which changes no rank that
matters).

{{< include ../../_generated/li-ceiling.md >}}

**Compare only within a row's sample.** On the held-out accounts the noise-free logit reaches
{{< var ceiling.li.latent_holdout >}}; the model falls short by
{{< var ceiling.li.gap_holdout >}} and gets {{< var ceiling.li.share_of_reach >}} of the way
from a coin toss to the ceiling. The ceiling barely depends on the one driver a bank could not
know at decision time: without the deterioration term it is
{{< var ceiling.li.latent_no_det_holdout >}}. Unlike Early Warning's, this label is
learnable: the noise is small, and the gate at {{< var li.gate.auc_min >}} sits below what the
data allow.

## Baselines: single inputs {#li-baselines}

The label's observable drivers are inputs ([8.2](data.qmd#li-label)), so the simplest offer
list is the book sorted by one of them. The table above compares the model with each, on the
same held-out accounts; each difference has a paired bootstrap interval
({{< var li.boot.n >}} resamples scoring both rankings on the same rows).

- **The model beats every single input.** Against `annual_revenue`, the best single numeric
  input by held-out AUC ({{< var li.baseline.best.auc >}}), its lead is
  {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff >}} with an interval of {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff_lo >}}
  to {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff_hi >}}. That best input was picked on these same held-out
  rows, which flatters it, so the model's lead is if anything understated. Against utilisation,
  the score's PD and Early Warning's probability the intervals lie further above zero.
- **No single input reaches the AUC gate.** All {{< var li.baseline.n_numeric >}} numeric
  inputs were tried alone, each oriented to rank the right way; the best reaches
  {{< var li.baseline.best.auc >}}.
- **{{< var li.baseline.n_pass_lift >}} of them pass the lift gate alone.** Sorted by
  utilisation, by revenue, by the balance, or by a column that restates one of them, the top fifth of the
  held-out accounts beats the base rate by at least {{< var li.gate.lift_min >}}×:
  utilisation reaches {{< var li.baseline.utilization.lift >}}× and revenue
  {{< var li.baseline.revenue.lift >}}×. The lift gate would pass a sort on one column, so it
  says little about the model; the AUC gate does the work (finding 3).
- **A low PD is not a good candidate.** The score's PD alone ranks this label at
  {{< var li.baseline.pd_score.auc >}}, and Early Warning's probability at
  {{< var li.baseline.ews.auc >}}: low risk and room to grow are different questions.

## Held out against the whole book {#li-held-out-vs-whole-book}

The portal scores the whole booked book. Over it the model looks far stronger:

{{< include ../../_generated/li-insample.md >}}

**Only the first row is a performance measure.** {{< var li.n_train >}} of the
{{< var li.n_book >}} booked accounts are training rows, on which the model is almost
perfect. The threshold is a quantile of the whole-book column, and every offer is chosen from
it (finding 2).

## The offered cohort {#li-cohort}

The offers are drawn from the whole book: {{< var li.offers.n_train >}} of the
{{< var li.n_offered >}} ({{< var li.offers.train_share >}}) are training rows, and
{{< var li.offers.n_holdout >}} are held out. Their outcomes, against the book's:

{{< include ../../_generated/li-cohort.md >}}

**The label rate among all offers is in-sample.** {{< var li.offers.rate >}} of offers are
positive, but most of them are rows whose label the model was fitted on. The held-out offers
are the honest measure: {{< var li.offers_ho.observed >}} positive against a mean probability
of {{< var li.offers_ho.predicted >}} — observed / predicted {{< var li.offers_ho.ratio >}},
{{< var li.offers_ho.status >}} on {{< var li.offers_ho.events >}} events, which clears the
monitoring floor of {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} — and
{{< var li.offers_ho.lift >}} times the book's base rate. Every held-out account above the
threshold, offered or not ({{< var li.thr_ho.n >}} accounts), gives observed
{{< var li.thr_ho.observed >}} against predicted {{< var li.thr_ho.predicted >}}, ratio
{{< var li.thr_ho.ratio >}}, {{< var li.thr_ho.status >}}. Calibration is judged against the
tolerance {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to {{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, counted only on
at least the floor's events, the same rule as D4, D5 and D7 ([8.8](monitoring.qmd)).

**Outcomes the label does not measure.** The cohort table also gives deterioration (Early
Warning's label) and default:

- Across all offers, {{< var li.offers.default.rate >}} default against
  {{< var li.book.default.rate >}} for the book — on only {{< var li.offers.default.events >}}
  defaults, below the floor, so it is recorded, not measured. Default is not this model's
  label, but the PD ceiling selects on the scorecard's estimate of it, so a low rate is what
  the rules are designed to give. On the held-out offers there are
  {{< var li.offers_ho.default.events >}} defaults.
- Offers deteriorate at {{< var li.offers.det.rate >}} ({{< var li.offers.det.events >}} of
  {{< var li.n_offered >}}) against {{< var li.book.det.rate >}} for the book. **That is not
  distinguishable from the book**: an exact binomial test against the book rate gives a
  p-value of {{< var li.offers.det.p_value >}}, and the 95% interval for the offers' rate runs
  from {{< var li.offers.det.ci_lo >}} to {{< var li.offers.det.ci_hi >}}. The held-out offers'
  {{< var li.offers_ho.det.rate >}} rests on {{< var li.offers_ho.det.events >}} events, below
  the floor (interval {{< var li.offers_ho.det.ci_lo >}} to {{< var li.offers_ho.det.ci_hi >}}).

## Offers by score band {#li-bands}

`segments` over the book, as the portal shows it:

{{< include ../../_generated/li-bands.md >}}

Band D gets no offers: its lowest PD, {{< var li.band.D.pd_min >}}, is above the ceiling of
{{< var li.offer_max_pd >}}, though {{< var li.band.D.amount_positive >}} of its accounts have
an amount. Band B gets the most, {{< var li.band.B.offers >}} offers and
\${{< var li.band.B.exposure >}} of assumed incremental exposure — the band in which the
scorecard under-predicts on the booked (D4 finding 6, [8.4](assumptions.qmd#li-the-score)).

## The economics of the offers {#li-economics}

{{< include ../../_generated/li-economics.md >}}

The offers clear the hurdle with little room on many: {{< var li.econ.n_near_hurdle >}} of
the {{< var li.n_offered >}} are within one point of it, and the lowest is
{{< var li.econ.roe_min >}}. The aggregate the gate tests is {{< var li.agg_roe >}}; with
every increase fully drawn it would be {{< var li.econ.full_draw.agg_roe >}}
([8.4](assumptions.qmd#li-drawdown)). The committed new limit,
\${{< var li.econ.amount_total >}}, is what the bank would extend; the
\${{< var li.econ.exposure_total >}} reported as exposure is that limit times today's
utilisation (finding 5).

## Offers on the Early Warning screen {#li-ews}

The two modules do not read each other, but the customer-360 view shows an offered account's
Early Warning tier and triggers beside the offer. Each measure on the offers, beside the same
measure over the whole book, computed as D7 computes its own:

{{< include ../../_generated/li-cohort-ews.md >}}

What the table shows, and what it does not:

- **By tier, the offers are flagged less than the book.** {{< var li.offers.ews.High.share >}}
  of offers are High-tier against {{< var li.book.ews.High.share >}} of the book, and
  {{< var li.offers.ews.high_or_medium.share >}} are High or Medium against
  {{< var li.book.ews.high_or_medium.share >}}. None is on Early Warning's default watchlist of the riskiest
  {{< var ews.watchlist.top_n_default >}}.
- **By trigger, they are flagged more, and the excess is largely mechanical.**
  {{< var li.offers.ews.any_trigger.share >}} carry at least one trigger against
  {{< var li.book.ews.any_trigger.share >}} of the book. Most of that is the two rules on
  utilisation: `HIGH_UTILIZATION` ({{< var li.offers.ews.trigger.high_utilization.share >}}
  against {{< var li.book.ews.trigger.high_utilization.share >}}) and `RISING_UTILIZATION`
  ({{< var li.offers.ews.trigger.rising_utilization.share >}} against
  {{< var li.book.ews.trigger.rising_utilization.share >}}). The offers are selected for high
  utilisation — an amount requires it — so they trip rules on utilisation by design.
  Excluding those two, {{< var li.offers.ews.non_util_trigger.share >}} of offers carry a
  trigger against {{< var li.book.ews.non_util_trigger.share >}} of the book. The triggers
  that are still more frequent among offers, `FREQUENT_OVERDRAFTS` and `DEPOSIT_DECLINE`,
  are drawn from utilisation in the generator too (`shared/data_generator.py`: overdrafts rise
  with utilisation above a level, deposits fall near the limit). `DELINQUENCY`, the one
  trigger the generator drives mainly by the true PD, fires
  on fewer offers than accounts in the book ({{< var li.offers.ews.trigger.delinquency.share >}}
  against {{< var li.book.ews.trigger.delinquency.share >}}).
- **Their deterioration is not distinguishable from the book's** (above).

The overlap is real and a reviewer will see it: an offer can arrive with a High tier or a
trigger beside it. On this evidence it is not a finding that the module offers to
deteriorating accounts; it is recorded as an observation, with the control that a reviewer
reads the Early Warning screen before an offer goes out
([8.7](limitations.qmd#li-observations)).

## What the portal serves {#li-served}

The portal's candidates endpoint serves the top {{< var li.served.portal.n >}} of
`candidates()` by default, and the v1 page shows {{< var li.served.page.n >}}. Of the
portal's {{< var li.served.portal.n >}}, {{< var li.served.portal.n_train >}} are training
rows and their label rate is {{< var li.served.portal.rate >}}; of the page's
{{< var li.served.page.n >}}, {{< var li.served.page.n_train >}} and
{{< var li.served.page.rate >}}. Those rates are the model remembering labels it was fitted on
(finding 2). The held-out offers' {{< var li.offers_ho.observed >}} is the figure to quote.

## Stability

No population stability index is computed for the model's features: the training and held-out
accounts are a random partition of one book, so a PSI between them would measure sampling
noise, and there is no second period (D4 finding 1). The share of held-out accounts above the
threshold, {{< var li.thr.share_holdout >}} against {{< var li.thr.share_book >}} intended, is
the one comparison of the in-sample calibration with new accounts; the monitoring plan carries
stability over time ([8.8](monitoring.qmd)).
